drivingQuestion: Is the blasphemer liable for the four-letter name, and only for it?
outcomeNote: both versions of Rav Aḥa's statement are defended against the charge of redundancy

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיְּבָרֵךְ שֵׁם בֶּן אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת, לְאַפּוֹקֵי בֶּן שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת דְּלָא.
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov says:» The blasphemer «is not liable unless he blesses,» i.e., curses, «the Tetragrammaton,» the four-letter name of God, which is «to the exclusion of» one who curses the «two-letter» name of God, spelled yod heh, «who is not» liable.

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! ״יַכֶּה יוֹסִי אֶת יוֹסִי״ תְּנַן? מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִילְּתָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּנָקֵט, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Isn’t that «obvious? We learned» in the mishna that the expression used in court is «let Yosei smite Yosei,» which indicates a four-letter name. The Gemara answers: «Lest you say» that the tanna «mentions» this «statement» as «a mere» example but does not intend that the witnesses use the four-letter name in particular, Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov «teaches us» that one is liable only for cursing the Tetragrammaton.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: שֵׁם בֶּן אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת נָמֵי שֵׁם הוּא.
segments.en: «There are» those «who say» that «Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov says» as follows: «Conclude from» the mishna that the «Tetragrammaton is also a name» for which one is liable, and he is liable not only for cursing the forty-two-letter name of God.

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא? ״יַכֶּה יוֹסִי אֶת יוֹסִי״ תְּנַן! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: עַד דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם רַבָּה, וּמִילְּתָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּנָקֵט – קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Isn’t that «obvious? We learned» in the mishna that the expression used in court is «let Yosei smite Yosei.» The Gemara answers: «Lest you say» that one is not liable «unless there is a grand name» that he curses, i.e., the forty-two-letter name, «and» the tanna «mentions» this «statement» as «a mere» example, Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov «teaches us» that one is liable even for cursing the Tetragrammaton, and the name Yosei is mentioned specifically.
